minutes.headline: Commission delayed the PJ Keating pump house decision pending state conditions; approved two projects, elected a vice chair and clerk.
minutes.summary: Acting chair Mary hosted after resigning as chair, and after Bob Peas resigned from the commission. Jenny was elected vice chair and Mike clerk; the chair seat was tabled. The commission heard several continued and new hearings, approved the Kevin Hill Landings and Sunny Hill Road notices of intent, approved several certificates of compliance, and approved a riding mower purchase.

public_comment.topic: Acting chair asked for public comment at the start; no hands were raised.
Mr Gibbons said he waited hours on the 20 Kilburn Chapter 61B item without knowing it had been voted on the week before.
Jay Simeon asked about the status of a property (45 or 52), and said his question was answered.

what_happened.line: The Commission continued the PJ Keating pump house decision to August after a straw poll favoured waiting for Natural Heritage conditions; the applicant agreed.
The Commission approved the 255 Sunny Hill Road notice of intent with a special condition that the 6-inch drain location be updated on the plan before installation.
The Commission approved the 791 Mass Ave notice of intent with standard conditions and approved five certificates of compliance.
The Commission elected a vice chair and a clerk by roll call and tabled the chair seat; the acting chair will keep hosting meetings.
The Commission approved spending up to a new total on a riding lawn mower for Hollis Road and the pollinator habitat, after the earlier purchase was specced as a tractor with no mowing deck.

why_it_matters: Wetlands decisions such as the PJ Keating pump house and Sunny Hill Road drainage set conditions on work near water, and a delay means those conditions are not yet fixed.
The Commission has no chair and has lost a member, which bears on how reliably its hearings can be scheduled and voted.
The mower purchase and the Mass Trails grant match draw on conservation money and possibly ARPA funds, which residents may be asked to support at the Select Board.
watch_next: The Commission's August 7 meeting, where PJ Keating, Village at Flat Hills, 390 Howard Street and the 60 Crossroad lots were continued.
Whether the Select Board agrees to use ARPA funds for the Mass Trails grant match, which the Commission endorsed asking for.

The one real difference to check is the PJ Keating continuance, which our minutes date to August 8th and which the official minutes do not show as a PJ Keating vote.
